## Conflicts

| temp-id | parties | contradiction | proposed resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| CF-061 | doc 2 §11 blueprint table ("Control envelope: … idempotency keys") / WS-F2 vs WS-B2 | Doc 2 files idempotency keys under the control envelope; this dossier derives the key inside the effect model from durable ledger state | Split: key *derivation* and the `dedup_support` contract belong to the effect model (WS-B2, C0); retry *policy* (attempt counts, backoff, budget) consumes the effect risk class and lives in the control envelope (WS-F2). Neither re-derives the other. |
| CF-062 | Managed Agents (S-047 "the model decides whether to retry"; Symphony S-108 adapters own idempotency) vs WS-B2 invariant 4 / ADR-2 | Production systems let the model or adapter decide retries; this dossier forbids automatic redispatch of `irreversible` effects and requires probe-before-retry for `compensable` | Both hold in their domains: model-decided retry is permitted for `read_only`/`reversible` (the only classes those systems operate on); the runtime enforces at-most-once for `irreversible` and probe-first for `compensable`. Record as conditionality in ADR-2 (d). |
| CF-063 | OpenHands SDK (S-110: model-supplied `security_risk` honoured as an approval input; `Agent.step()` re-executes unmatched actions) vs WS-B2 monotone classification rule and invariant 4 | A precedent harness both trusts model self-report as a risk input and replays unobserved actions | Adopt OpenHands' *shape* (`UNKNOWN` incomparable; `confirm_unknown`), not its trust order: self-report may only *raise* the class; unobserved actions are never replayed without a probe or an idempotent class. Flag the replay path as an anti-pattern in the spec's failure-modes list. |
| CF-064 | WS-B2 event family vs WS-B1 event taxonomy table | WS-B1 lists `action.effect.intent/prepared/committed/observed`; WS-B2 needs six further classes (`refused, unknown, probed, compensated, reverted, abandoned`) and adds `effect_id` + `effective_risk_class` to `security.permission.decided` | Coordination, not contradiction: synthesis adds the six classes to WS-B1's table under producer "effect layer (B2)" with `durability = ledger`, and the two payload fields to `security.permission.decided`. WS-B2 adopts B1's names, envelope, `fencing_token` and `effect_ledger` projection unchanged. |
| CF-065 | WS-A3 `EffectClass` (closed sum of effect *kinds*: `read_fs, write_fs, exec, net_egress, …`; ontology term "effect class") vs WS-B2 draft's "effect class" (reversibility × repeat-safety × scope) | One term for two orthogonal concepts | WS-A3 keeps `EffectClass`/"effect class" = kind. WS-B2's triple is renamed **effect risk class** (`declared_risk_class`, `effective_risk_class`); the `Effect` record carries both `effect_kind: EffectClass` and the risk class. Ontology row below. |
| CF-066 | WS-B1 §6.3 `action.effect.*` payload `reversibility ∈ {reversible, compensable, irreversible}` and phase name `committed` vs WS-B2 §6.2 four-value reversibility and write-ahead semantics | B1's enum lacks `read_only` (needed to skip the write-ahead barrier); B1's `committed` could be read as "applied" | Add `read_only` to the enum in B1's payload (B2 owns the semantics; B1 owns the field); document in the spec that `committed` = "commit record durable before dispatch" and `observed(applied)` = "applied". Also correct B1 F9's "four-state" ACP status to five (`cancelled`). |

## Ontology terms

| term | definition | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **effect** | The runtime's unit of side-effect accounting: one attempt-independent identity (`effect_id`) for one semantic action the harness intends to perform on an environment or the outside world; one tool call may yield several effects (`parent_effect_id`). Runtime record, distinct from the IR type `EffectClass`. | WS-B2 (semantics) / WS-A3 (record shape) / WS-B1 (`EffectId`). CF-035. |
| **effect intent** | The opening lifecycle record of an effect (`action.effect.intent`): what the harness proposes to do, with canonical argument hash and declared risk class, before authorization. | Shepherd (S-078) "intent"/"outcome" pair precedent. |
| **effect phase** | One of the lifecycle states `intended, authorized/refused, prepared, committed, observed, unknown, probed, compensated, reverted, abandoned`. | Co-owned with WS-B1 (`effect phase` term). |
| **effect risk class** | The triple `{reversibility ∈ {read_only, reversible, compensable, irreversible}, repeat_safety ∈ {idempotent, non_idempotent}, scope ∈ {workspace_local, external}}` declared on a `ToolCapability` and re-assessed per effect. Orthogonal to `EffectClass` (kind). | Resolves CF-065. |
| **reversibility** (of an effect) | Whether a prior state can be restored mechanically from a baseline (`reversible`), only semantically by a registered compensator (`compensable`), or not at all (`irreversible`); `read_only` = no world change. | Shepherd (S-078), Revisable-by-Design (S-205) taxonomies. |
| **repeat safety** | Whether re-executing an effect with the same canonical arguments has no additional effect (`idempotent`) or does (`non_idempotent`). | MCP `idempotentHint` semantics (S-153). |
| **effect scope** | `workspace_local` (inside an environment handle the runtime can snapshot/discard) vs `external` (open world). | MCP `openWorldHint` (S-153). |
| **effective risk class** | `max_by_danger(kernel_assessed, declared)`; `unknown` ⇒ `{irreversible, non_idempotent, external}`; model self-report and untrusted server hints may raise but never lower it. | Kernel decision input (WS-H1), approval default input (WS-H7). |
| **effect outcome** | The result recorded at `observed`: `applied`, `not_applied`, `partial`; or the non-terminal `unknown` with a cause. | |
| **write-ahead commit record** | The durable `action.effect.committed` event that must precede executor dispatch for every non-`read_only` effect; lets recovery distinguish "never dispatched" from "dispatched, outcome unknown". | Sagas coordinator checkpointing (S-197). |
| **probe (verify-before-retry)** | A read-only operation that establishes whether an `unknown` effect was applied (`applied / not_applied / undeterminable`) before any redispatch. | S-204 mechanism; Symphony reconciliation (S-108). |
| **idempotency key** | `H(run_id, effect_id, canonical(args), capability_version)` — stable across attempts and restarts; presented to executors/targets that support dedup. | Stripe (S-200), Helland (S-199). |
| **dedup support** | An executor/target capability value `∈ {none, executor, target}` with a `dedup_window`; determines whether at-least-once dispatch becomes effectively-once. | |
| **fencing token** | The strictly increasing per-scope token carried by every post-`prepared` effect event; the ledger rejects stale tokens (`Fenced`). At C0 it is the run writer lease's token. | Co-owned with WS-B1 (`writer lease / fencing token`); OpenHands `generation` precedent. |
| **compensation plan / compensating effect** | A registered, idempotent, kernel-authorisable template that semantically undoes a `compensable` effect; executed as a new effect with a `compensates` edge, in reverse commit order. | Sagas (S-197). |
| **revert effect / baseline** | A mechanical restoration of a `reversible` effect from its `baseline_ref` (snapshot, git, per-path baseline), recorded as a new effect with a `reverts` edge. | Codex `turn_diff_tracker.rs`; WS-B4. |
| **detached effect** | A child effect (background process, spawned job) that continues after its parent is `observed` or `unknown`; recorded in `detached_effect_ids[]` and kept under the run's lease. | Codex unified exec precedent. |
| **abandoned effect** | Terminal state for an effect whose compensation failed or whose `unknown` outcome cannot be resolved automatically; always escalated and audited; blocks or annotates completion (OQ-092). | |
| **at-least-once dispatch / at-most-once dispatch / effectively-once** | The only delivery promises the spec makes: at-least-once dispatch for `read_only`/`reversible`; at-most-once dispatch for non-repeat-safe effects without dedup support; effectively-once when dispatch is deduplicated by key. "Exactly-once effect" is never claimed. | Helland (S-199). |
